claims.text: The initial material is an as-deposited, homogeneous, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi high-entropy-alloy film.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi film has an ordered, single-phase hexagonal structure.
The homogeneous FeMnNiGeSi baseline undergoes a sharp, hysteretic, first-order magnetostructural transition.
Magnetron sputtering can be used to produce multicomponent films with controlled compositional gradients.
Alternating approximately 10 nm layers with small Mn or Ge differences can create nanoscale compositional modulation in FeMnNiGeSi films.
The ordered hexagonal phase can be preserved while fabricating a compositionally modulated FeMnNiGeSi film a few hundred nanometers thick.
Nanoscale compositional gradients generate localized strain fields at interfaces between layers.
Nanoscale compositional gradients modulate magnetic exchange interactions at interfaces between layers.
Built-in strain gradients spatially distribute the nucleation and progression of the magnetostructural transition across the film.
A spatially distributed magnetostructural transition lowers the energy barrier for reversal.
Lowering the reversal barrier broadens and smooths the magnetocaloric response under low applied fields.
Lowering the reversal barrier reduces hysteresis under low applied fields.
The compositionally modulated multilayer will maintain a significant entropy change despite transition broadening.
Relative to a homogeneous as-deposited film, the multilayer film will exhibit a broader magnetocaloric transition during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Relative to a homogeneous as-deposited film, the multilayer film will exhibit reduced hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The film's enhanced surface-to-volume ratio may promote more rapid heat exchange.
The predicted effects apply over temperatures where the ordered hexagonal phase remains stable and for layer thicknesses near 10 nm.
Excessive compositional contrast or interlayer mixing may suppress the intended strain modulation and cause the predicted effects to fail.
Grain boundaries may affect transition broadening and hysteresis independently of the proposed compositional-modulation mechanism.
